messages:
emily: customer reported that their free-trial credits didn't go down after several successful generation calls. they show 3 successful responses but balance unchanged. account: acct_8t9z, customer email: team@example.com

emily: here's the curl they used, internal support copy:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-user-abc' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 2025-09-30T12:11:22Z' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}'
```

emily: response body was normal (text output). response headers included `x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c` and `x-tokens-used: 0` per customer. they attached a screenshot.

marie: can you paste the full response headers / request id? I want to look at runtime logs for rq_0a1b2c

emily: pasted below from customer screenshot: `x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c, x-tokens-used: 0, x-cache-status: HIT`

raj: interesting — `x-cache-status: HIT` and `x-tokens-used: 0` suggests we served from prefix cache but didn't emit billing event. forwarding to billing infra.

hao: pulling events for acct_8t9z around 2025-09-30T12:11:22Z... i see the runtime handled the request and returned 200 for rq_0a1b2c. there is no corresponding usage_event in the billing queue for that request id.

marie: any recent changes to caching pipeline? i recall a refactor that moved cache short-circuit earlier in the path.

raj: yes, last week we merged `cache-eager-return` (PR #3821). it short-circuits response generation when prefix hit, returns cached text before the meter/decorate middleware executes. that would explain 0 tokens and no usage_event.

marie: oh. that PR was supposed to call meter.emit on cache hits but i see a conditional early-return slipped in. bug.

marie: proposed fix: ensure `await meter.emitUsage(req, respMeta)` is invoked in the cache-return path — small hotfix. i'll open a rollback/hotfix PR now.

deploy-bot: new deployment requested by marie — hotfix/cache-billing-emit (diff: +3 -1). queued for canary in us-west-2.

hao: i'll run a quick scan for other accounts with `x-cache-status: HIT` and missing usage_event between 2025-09-24..2025-09-30. rough count: ~142 affected requests across 12 accounts.

emily: customer impacted count: they show 3 calls in the screenshot — can we confirm how many of their requests were affected and credit amount?

raj: checking token accounting for cached responses is tricky b/c cached responses may correspond to prior generation cost. but our billing model charges on response serve, so we must bill on cache-hit as well. for acct_8t9z i see 3 missed usage_events totalling ~115 tokens.

hao: after hotfix deploy, i'll backfill usage_events for the missing request ids and emit ledger entries. planning a reconciliation script: backfill_usage(account_id, [rq ids]) -> create usage_event -> ledger_process.

marie: hotfix deployed to canary, tests green. rolling to prod now.

deploy-bot: deployment completed to prod (hotfix/cache-billing-emit) at 2025-10-01T01:22:15Z.

hao: backfill script executed for the 12 accounts. acct_8t9z received 115 tokens debited and a note in audit log: "reconciled missing billing due to cache-path bug (PR #3821)". ledger txn: lg_tx_77k.

emily: updated customer — i told them we found a bug where cached responses bypassed billing emission after a recent refactor, we've debited the missing 115 tokens and added a credit note for transparency. customer asked for proof, i've attached tx id and audit note. they asked for a goodwill credit to offset confusion.

raj: mba - recommend we grant a one-time goodwill credit of 200 tokens for acct_8t9z. also add alerting for cache-hit without usage_event. i'll file an observability ticket.

hao: filed INFRA-5623: alert if cache-hit AND no usage_event emitted within 5s.

marie: postmortem stub created, assigning owners. root cause: premature early-return after cache-hit removed meter.emit call. mitigation: hotfix (done), backfill (done), alert (INFRA-5623), postmortem + stricter code review checklist for middleware ordering.

emily: customer accepted reconciliation and goodwill credit, thanks everyone. closing case. :white_check_mark:
